# pbs_api_token (Resource)

Manages an API token of a PBS user.

The token secret is returned by PBS only when the token is created (or regenerated) and is stored
in the Terraform state as the sensitive attribute `value`. Treat the state accordingly.

* To issue a new secret without replacing the token (its ACLs are kept), change `regenerate_trigger`
  from one non-null value to another. Setting it for the first time (e.g. after import) or removing it
  only records the change and keeps the current secret. Regeneration requires PBS 3.3.7 or later.
* After `terraform import` the secret is unknown, so `value` is null until the token is regenerated.
* A token only has the privileges granted to it via ACLs (see `pbs_acl`), intersected with those of its user.
* Deleting the token also deletes its ACL entries; deleting the owning user deletes all of its tokens.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pbs_user" "backup" {
  userid  = "backup@pbs"
  comment = "Automation user"
}

resource "pbs_api_token" "backup" {
  userid     = pbs_user.backup.userid
  token_name = "terraform"
  comment    = "Used by backup clients"

  # Optional: disable the token or let it expire (Unix epoch seconds, 0 = never).
  # enable = false
  # expire = 1893456000

  # Change this value to issue a new secret in place (token and ACLs are kept).
  # Adding or removing the attribute does not regenerate the secret.
  regenerate_trigger = "2026-01"
}

# Tokens only get privileges explicitly granted to them.
resource "pbs_acl" "backup_token" {
  path    = "/datastore/backups"
  auth_id = pbs_api_token.backup.tokenid
  role    = "DatastoreBackup"
}

output "backup_token_secret" {
  value     = pbs_api_token.backup.value
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `token_name` (String) Name of the token (3-64 characters, letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `-`; must not start with `.` or `-`). The full token ID `userid!token_name` may not exceed 64 characters. Changing this forces a new token.
- `userid` (String) User that owns the token, e.g. `backup@pbs`. Changing this forces a new token.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Comment (single line, at most 128 characters).
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the token is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
- `expire` (Number) Expiration date as Unix epoch seconds. `0` (default) means the token never expires.
- `regenerate_trigger` (String) Arbitrary value; when it changes from one non-null value to another, the token secret is regenerated in place (the token and its ACLs are kept). Setting it on create, adding it to an existing token (e.g. after import) or removing it does not regenerate the secret; the current secret is kept and only the new trigger value is recorded.

### Read-Only

- `tokenid` (String) Full token ID (`userid!token_name`), used as auth ID for ACLs and as API token user.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The token secret. Only known after create or regeneration; null after import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# API tokens are imported by their full ID "user@realm!tokenname".
# The secret cannot be read back, so `value` is null after import.
# Adding `regenerate_trigger` to the configuration afterwards only records its
# value and keeps the current secret; change it again to issue a new secret
# (stored in `value`). Removing the trigger never regenerates the secret.
terraform import pbs_api_token.backup 'backup@pbs!terraform'
```
